sections.title: Conditional probability: choose the reference group

blocks.text: **Conditional probability:** P(A | B) = count in both A and B / count in B. Read it as “the probability of A among B.” The restricted group B is the denominator; P(A | B) and P(B | A) usually differ. Assumes equally weighted cases and a non-empty reference group.

blocks.setup: One table; rows are commute status and columns are cycling status.

steps.label: Counts
steps.text: Among 25 commuters, 10 cycle; among 15 noncommuters, 5 cycle. Total cyclists = 15; total noncyclists = 25.

steps.label: Row %: cycle among commuters
steps.text: Reference group = commuters, so divide by the commuter row total: 10 / 25 = 40.0% of commuters.

steps.label: Column %: commuters among cyclists
steps.text: Reference group = cyclists, so divide by the cyclist column total: 10 / 15 = 66.7% of cyclists.

steps.label: Check
steps.text: Row percentages add to 100% across each row. Column percentages add to 100% down each column. Across a row of column percentages, they need not add to 100%.

blocks.takeaway: Name the group after “among” first; use its row or column total as denominator.

blocks.text: **Exam reporting:** give every proportion as a percentage rounded to 1 decimal place and name the reference group: “40.0% of commuters.”

Split cases by a categorical variable; compute one summary (such as a mean or count) per non-empty group. Output: one row per group, not per original case. Compare the same kind of summary across groups; do not compare a mean with a total.
